claims.claim: The agent command used was `node claude_md_gen.js --project-root /tmp/eval-i3-cmd-preserve --wiki-root /tmp/eval-i3-cmd-preserve/wiki --update /tmp/eval-i3-cmd-preserve/CLAUDE.md`

claims.claim: The managed block is substantive, not an error stub or whitespace-only filler
claims.evidence: 366 bytes with 4 real `##` headings, a wiki link, and project-name interpolation.

suggestions.reason: No assertion verifies that the file ends with exactly one trailing newline (or that the last line is not duplicated). The current suite would still pass if the regenerator introduced a phantom trailing newline or stripped one, because the post-region byte-equality assertion happens to cover only what's below the end marker — but this is correct here by coincidence. Consider an explicit `len(file) == len(pre)+len(managed)+len(post)` round-trip check, or a final-byte check.

No assertion verifies that the pre/post regions' content, if they happened to also contain a literal `<!-- wiki-managed: start -->` string (e.g., inside a fenced code block), would not confuse the parser. The current input avoids this, so the test doesn't discriminate a naive substring-based implementation from a proper one. A more discriminating fixture would place the literal marker text inside a fenced code block in the user's manual header and confirm it's preserved verbatim.
suggestions.assertion: After regeneration, the file still contains exactly one `<!-- wiki-managed: start -->` and one `<!-- wiki-managed: end -->` marker
The refreshed managed section contains substantive content: at least one heading AND either a link into wiki/ or a mention of the project's real name
suggestions.reason: The OR is satisfied trivially here because the generator emits both branches. Consider tightening to AND, or require a link target that actually resolves inside the wiki root (not just the literal substring `wiki/`). Current assertion would also pass for a hardcoded template that always says `[Wiki documentation](wiki/index.md)` regardless of wiki content.

eval_feedback.overall: Evals are strong and well-chosen: the 3-region SHA-256 split with byte-exact before/after equality on pre and post, plus a 'must differ' hash on managed, is a good discriminating design that genuinely exercises the preservation guarantee. The marker-count + whitespace-drift check and the idempotency check round out the suite well. The one real gap is that the OR in the content-substance check is trivially satisfied by a static template; tightening it to require a heading whose wiki-link target is actually a real file under `wiki/` would be more discriminating.
